rankings.reasoning: Concrete and reproducible bypass of protocol-destination screening in RaffleFactory._validateCreateParams and Raffle.initialize using a deterministic future Clones.clone CREATE address as sponsorRecipient. Once the sibling Raffle clone is deployed and registered in isRaffle, _transferQuote in releaseSponsorProceeds permanently reverts with InvalidQuoteDestination (locking sponsorProceeds in the contract), while releaseSponsorPrize uses unscreened transferFrom and moves the prize NFT directly into the sibling Raffle clone, violating the design invariant against moving assets between raffle clones. Ranked Low rather than Medium because sponsorRecipient is sponsor-chosen at creation and does not affect winner payouts, buyer refunds, or protocol treasury fees.
rankings.root_bug: Precomputed future Raffle clone CREATE addresses bypass time-of-creation isRaffle and code-length destination screening in _validateCreateParams and _isProtocolDestination before the sibling clone is deployed

rankings.reasoning: Reproducible bypass of Raffle._update ticket destination hygiene using the same precomputed future Raffle clone CREATE address mechanism during buyEntries (or pre-deployment ticket transfers), since _isProtocolDestination skips canonicalFactory.isRaffle when to.code.length == 0 and ERC721._safeMint skips onERC721Received for codeless recipients. Ranked below Finding 1 with reduced reward because it shares the same underlying root cause and a buyer can already strand their own ticket and claim by minting or transferring to any unowned address without impacting other participants' refunds, sponsor payouts, or treasury fees.
rankings.root_bug: Precomputed future Raffle clone CREATE addresses bypass time-of-creation isRaffle and code-length destination screening in _validateCreateParams and _isProtocolDestination before the sibling clone is deployed

summary: Ranked 2 target findings in full_rerank mode. Both findings exploit the time-of-check vs. time-of-use gap in protocol-destination screening (_isProtocolDestination and _validateCreateParams) where deterministic future ERC-1167 CREATE clone addresses have code.length == 0 and isRaffle == false until a subsequent createRaffle call deploys them. Finding 1 is ranked first (#1, Low) because setting sponsorRecipient to a future clone address causes a permanent revert in releaseSponsorProceeds and transfers the returned prize NFT into a sibling Raffle clone via releaseSponsorPrize. Finding 3 is ranked second (#2, Low) as a lower-impact variant of the same root cause affecting buyer-specified ticket recipients.
